claim: After learning 三日 as 'Three days' and 二日間 as 'Two days', a learner reads 一日 as 'one day', and the back teaches tsuitachi with no hint that 'one day' is a different reading, so the learner comes away thinking 一日 is always tsuitachi.
evidence: Reading back: '一日 / Answer: The 1st (day of the month) / Says: tsuitachi'. Earlier cards: '三日 | Three days' (chapter-17), '二日間 | Two days' (chapter-16). 一 card gives only 'ichi, it-, itsu / hito'.
fix: Add a note that 一日 read as tsuitachi is the 1st of the month, and that the same characters meaning 'one day' are read ichinichi.

claim: The date cards gloss N日 only as 'The Nth (day of the month)', while the previous unit taught 三日 with the same kind of reading as 'Three days', so a learner who answers 四日 as 'four days' cannot tell from the back whether that was wrong.
evidence: Reading backs: '四日 / The 4th (day of the month) / yokka', '五日 / The 5th (day of the month) / itsuka', '十日 / The 10th (day of the month) / tōka'. Earlier: '三日 | Three days' (chapter-17).
fix: Gloss the 2nd to 10th and 20th as 'The Nth (day of the month); N days', or add a short note saying the same word counts days.

claim: 才 and 天才 both answer 'Genius', so the learner cannot see what 天 adds to the compound, and nothing links 才 to 歳, which was taught with the same reading and the same 'years old' meaning.
evidence: Reading back: '才 / Answer: Genius; years old / Says: sai'. Same unit: '天才 / Answer: Genius / Says: tensai'. Earlier: '歳 | Age; years old' (pronunciation sai, chapter-16).
fix: Gloss 才 as 'Talent; years old' (or 'Talent, genius; years old') and add a note that 才 is the simpler character often written for 歳 in ages.
